prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for its experimental discovery in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B044 as a single-part prize and I have not changed my preferred configuration since round 1. The scientific core is a nameable phenomenon in nature that was predicted from symmetry and band structure and then observed: Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry and strong spin-orbit coupling allow a Z2-classified insulator with protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's group measured the quantised edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe wells. The classification then became a working tool for electronic-structure theory. Bulk invariants, parity-based diagnostics and first-principles searches for new compounds all follow from it, and ARPES and transport groups use the surface and edge states routinely. Independent confirmation over nearly two decades has left the interpretation stable. The chair's summary shows four members preferring it and no file calling it premature or unconfirmed. I read the citation question the chair posed as the main task for this round, and I propose wording that claims the two-dimensional prediction and the HgTe discovery and does not claim the three-dimensional work, which the supplied credit cannot carry. I also keep the 2016 distinction: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were honoured for topological phase transitions and for topological phases in the quantum Hall and Haldane-model lineage, whereas the time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulator is a symmetry-protected class without a magnetic field and with a different experimental signature.
statement.case_against: The credit remains incomplete and I will not hide that. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe/CdTe as the platform and the band inversion that told Molenkamp where to look, and the three-dimensional contributors (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; Roy; Hsieh and Hasan) are outside the supplied set. Within a three-person limit, the citation must therefore be narrow, and a reader could still say the prize underweights the proposal for the concrete material. Further, Lindroth and Mehlig are right that a committee could regard the topological theme as partly recognised in 2016, and I cannot show that every colleague will accept the distinction I draw. Finally, B024 has the cleaner credit, and a prize judged only on cleanliness of attribution would favour it. I weigh B044 above it because I think the breadth of consequence and the decisive prediction-then-experiment structure outweigh an attribution gap that is a limit of the supplied names and not an error in the physics.

responses.point: Danielsson holds B044 first, treats the 2016 objection as weak because Z2 insulators are a distinct symmetry-protected class, and states that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang allocation problem cannot be resolved from the supplied names alone.
responses.response: I agree with all three parts and would answer the chair's wording question in the way your own citation suggests. The citation should name the prediction of the time-reversal-invariant state and the observation of it in HgTe wells, so that it is silent on who proposed the specific material and on the three-dimensional phases. That wording is defensible only because Molenkamp's measurement of the edge conductance is the first direct evidence for the state, and I would not let it be read as a ruling on priority for the HgTe proposal. Your broader citation, 'topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect', is the point where I differ. It would implicitly cover the three-dimensional class, whose contributors we cannot credit, so I prefer the narrower version.

responses.point: Lindroth holds B024 first for its crisp invention and clean two-name credit, and says the 2016 prize reduces the novelty of B044 and that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang allocation is unresolved. She asks that the clock citation stress invention and realisation because tests of constants so far set limits only.
responses.response: Your distinction between delivered capability and prospective new physics is fair, and it is the reason I would also word a clock citation around invention and realisation. On the 2016 point I hold my view, but I will answer your specific question. For time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators, the 2016 citation does not apply directly, because the Haldane model and the integer quantum Hall states break time-reversal symmetry, and the Kane-Mele invariant is defined for a time-reversal-symmetric system with spin-orbit coupling. Evidence that would change my mind would be a showing that the quantum spin Hall result is conceptually a corollary of the 2016 work and not a separate symmetry class, and I do not believe that is the case. I accept that attribution cleanliness favours your candidate, and I treat B024 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Kroll holds B024 first, argues that a roughly two-orders-of-magnitude capability gain is itself the source of new physics, and treats the two-name credit as complete. He ranked B044 fifth and describes it as outside his specialism.
responses.response: You make the strongest version of the case for a measurement invention, and I accept that a step change in capability can matter more than a single observation. The test I apply is what has already changed in other fields, and for lattice clocks the answer is mostly a capability and a set of limits, while the redefinition of the second is still ahead. For B044 the changed practice already exists in materials theory and spectroscopy. I would also resist the suggestion that attribution cleanliness decides between the two. The clock credit is cleaner, but it does not settle which achievement is the larger one, and I have moved B024 to the top of my alternatives because I take your case seriously. Pairing B044 with B024 would be five people, which exceeds the three-person cap, so I do not propose it.

responses.point: Mehlig holds B016 first for conceptual novelty about a basic law, and says the attribution problem in B044 is not minor because the HgTe proposal and the three-dimensional work lie outside the credited set. He lists the omission of Crooks in B016 as its own weakness.
responses.response: I agree the attribution problem is not minor, and I have written the case against around it. We differ on what follows. Any three-person set from B016 drops a decisive contributor and the choice among Jarzynski, Evans, Crooks and Seifert has no natural boundary. For B044 the boundary is defensible with narrow wording, because Kane and Mele are the prediction and Molenkamp is the discovery in the stated system. The omitted people are connected to a neighbouring result (the material proposal, the three-dimensional phases) and not to the achievement the citation names. I also take your point on fundamentality seriously. The exact fluctuation relations are a statement about a basic law, but they do not have a single decisive experimental discovery, which is what the committee can anchor a citation to in B044.

responses.point: Pearce proposes a two-part prize pairing B024 with B019, containing three laureates, and says the main weakness is that Halzen is the sole credited name for a collaboration of hundreds, which is why B044 is only an alternative for the chair.
responses.response: I follow the logic of a two-part prize with three names, and I agree the clock part is sound. I cannot support B019 as the second part. Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll each raised the sole-laureate problem, and the supplied credit gives us nothing wider, so we would be rewarding one person for a result that depended on the collaboration and on the AMANDA builders. You also noted that the source-level evidence for TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still developing. I would leave a configuration that avoids both problems. B044 alone has the strongest support in the file, and if the committee wants a second part I would rather see it chosen by scientific weight than by the count of laureates it adds.

responses.point: Johansson moved from B042 to B044, would limit the claim to the prediction and the HgTe quantum-well discovery, and sees Molenkamp as the only experimentalist in the credited set.
responses.response: We are now aligned on the wording, and I accept your restriction to the two-dimensional effect. I would add that Molenkamp is a defensible experimental credit within the supplied names because his group made the HgTe wells and reported the edge-channel transport, but I would not describe him as the only possible experimental name. The citation should say 'in HgTe quantum wells' so the experimental half is tied to a specific system and a specific measurement. I also note your recusal on B042, which is not part of my configuration, so it does not affect my position.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the 2016 prize does not cover time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators. I regard them as a distinct symmetry class, but Lindroth and Mehlig may read the topological theme as one, and I cannot settle this by argument alone.

Whether a citation limited to the two-dimensional prediction and the HgTe discovery is a fair account of the field, given that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the three-dimensional work lie outside the credited names.

Whether a clean two-name credit (B024) should outweigh breadth of consequence (B044) for members who regard unresolved attribution as disqualifying. I treat the gap as a limit of the supplied trio, not a disqualifier, but that is a judgment and not a measurable fact.
I rely on my own recollection of the history and have not verified fine points of priority, including the dates of the HgTe proposal and of the Molenkamp measurement.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional conflict with any credited person for B044 is documented in my profile. I retain the round-1 field-proximity flag for B037 and, to a lesser extent, B020, since electronic-structure theory, DFT and correlated electrons are my own research area. B037 is only an alternative in my position and B020 is not in my configuration. Johansson's declared recusal on B042 does not affect my position.
